question: Does the per-assay position R2 survive when whole position pairs, not random pairs, are held out?

rule.statistic: per-assay out-of-fold r2_resid_var (epsceil.baseline.r2_resid_var) at the outer-selected ridge lambda, under the whole_position_pair split, compared with the same assay under the random_pair split
rule.evaluated_for: position and pair_rank3, on all assays and within each n_cells bin (2, 3-9, >=10)
rule.ratio: median over the stratum's assays of whole-pair R2 / median of random-pair R2 (same assays)
rule.beats_null: share of the stratum's assays whose whole-pair R2 exceeds the mean of its own permutation nulls by > 1e-9
rule.INCONCLUSIVE: fewer than 6 assays in the stratum, or median random-pair R2 <= 0 (ratio undefined)
rule.order: INCONCLUSIVE, then HOLDS, then COLLAPSES, else PARTIAL (HOLDS and COLLAPSES are mutually exclusive)
rule.paired_difference: per-assay (whole-pair R2 - random-pair R2); median with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval over assays (5000 resamples, seed 20261116); reported, not used by the rule
rule.written: before any R2 under either split was computed

design.models: epsceil.baseline position and pair_rank{1,2,3}, unchanged; random_pair predictions come from crossfit_assay itself
design.whole_position_pair: GroupKFold(min(5, n_cells)) with one group per unordered position pair; leave-one-cell-out when an assay has < 5 cells
design.lambda: alt_baseline.outer_selection, run separately per split, for the real fits and for every permutation
design.metric: epsceil.baseline.r2_resid_var, out of fold, pooled over the assay's folds
design.null: 10 permutations per assay: residuals permuted among the training pairs of each inner fold (alt_baseline._rng), scored against the real held-out residuals
design.positions_seen: for each held-out pair under whole_position_pair: how many of its two positions occur in that fold's training pairs (a position never seen in training has alpha = 0, so the model can only fall back to the intercept)

position_pairs_per_assay.note: bimodal: most assays with < 10 cells have doubles at only a few position pairs (2 disjoint cells in the smallest bin), so a whole-pair holdout there predicts cells whose positions are largely unseen; read R2 by bin, not as one median
